description:
PR workflow for an AI-review-gated Lean repo (TauCeti): never open a PR that has not already passed the review rubric locally.

0. SOURCES BEFORE CODE. Before writing any new Lean, check every source the project roadmap names for the content (upstream research repos, sibling formalisation projects such as FLT) and pinned Mathlib itself. Mathlib absence requires an untruncated full-name grep AND a compiled `example` probing the generic routes (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective, constructor .injEq, exact?) — a name grep plus a statement grep together still missed three duplicates in one file, because Mathlib supplies facts generically via typeclasses and auto-generated lemmas that appear as text nowhere. Port and adapt; do not rederive.

1. GENUINELY NEW CODE ONLY: plan with /develop, execute with /beastmode, and run /mathlibable on the headline declarations.

2. ALWAYS, ported or new: full /cleanup on the file, and check whether /decompose-proof is needed (any proof over 30 lines; hard cap 50).

3. CI GATES locally: lake build, plus the repo's audit executables and lint script.

4. LOCAL RUBRIC DRY-RUN, NO PR YET. The review engine (TauCetiReview's runner/review.py, backed by ChatGPT models via the codex CLI — the same models CI draws) accepts --diff-file/--pr-desc-file/--no-post, so it runs on a LOCAL BRANCH with no PR in existence: stage code/ (git archive of the branch head), a FRESH roadmap clone (a stale local roadmap checkout produced a false scope BLOCK), mathlib/ (symlink to the project's pinned .lake/packages/mathlib), diff.txt (merge-base diff vs origin/main) and pr_desc.txt, then invoke the engine with --no-post --mode manual. Nothing touches GitHub. For API-design questions (which shape the reviewer will prefer), ask the same model beforehand via the ask_chatgpt_math MCP.

5. ITERATE step 4 UNTIL EVERY RUBRIC IS GREEN; only then gh pr create — at that point the PR is known to pass. The body carries the roadmap attribution line, the exact layer/target, full provenance (source repo, license, pinned revision, file and declaration names) and the project's machine-readable target marker, kept in sync with the code.

6. NEVER WAIT AROUND. A 10-minute cron checks open PRs for reviews/movement (reading the scoreboard states/head_sha, never the label); between server rounds, take the next candidates through steps 0-5 locally, so a queue of locally-green branches is always ready while earlier ones merge.
